newsitem.title: JAPAN: WEEK AHEAD - Tokyo stocks to drift in limited band.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - Tokyo stocks to drift in limited band.

text.p: The Tokyo stock market's key index is likely to drift in a limited range this week due to two separate trends in major sectors, brokers said.

Shares in banks and property-related firms are expected to stay under selling pressure amid lingering worries about their bad loan problems. Securities houses are also seen vulnerable to further developments in the Nomura Securities scandal.
But blue-chip shares in the high-tech and electrical sectors are expected to extend gains, backed by strong earnings prospects, they said.
On Friday, the market's benchmark 225-share Nikkei average closed at 17,860.59, down 329.13 points or 1.8 percent from March 28.
Many brokers expected the Nikkei average to hover between 17,500 and 18,500 this week.

"Sales including dissolution of mutual shareholdings will likely continue, especially in debt-laden financial and construction sectors. But blue-chip issues are likely to keep on rising on foreign investor buying," said Yoshihiro Itoh, general manager at Okasan Securities Co Ltd.

The securities sector is likely to remain weak, undermined by worries about the sector after Nomura Securities said last month that two directors were involved in suspected illegal deals in which Nomura money was moved to the account of a client, brokers said.
The market is still cautious about the recent corrective phase of U.S. stocks, but Wall Street's impact on Tokyo stocks is becoming muted, brokers said.

"The market is eyeing stocks in New York, which have been entering into an adjustment phase, but the Tokyo market has been more undaunted by the outside environment," said Masao Ariga, general manager at Daiwa Securities Co Ltd.
On Friday, Tokyo stocks closed moderately lower, mainly depressed by continuing weakness in the brokerage and construction sectors.
But despite losses in those sectors, some export-oriented firms in the high-tech and electrical sectors soared.
